text:
kai: quick sync — I bumped into a TP perf regression on the 8xA100 job. end-to-end latency up ~18% between yesterday and last week. profiling points to all-reduce stalls when message sizes hit ~512KB-2MB. anyone else observed a similar knee?
marta: yep spotted that on the 4/8-gpu scaling tests. ring microbenchmarks show a clear bandwidth drop in that region. seems like message size puts us out of efficient ring utilization.
samir: ran nccl-tests earlier, reproduced. attaching the snippet of the microbenchmark I ran:
```
# nccl-tests allreduce sweep (shortened)
./all_reduce_perf -b 64K -e 4M -f 2 -g 8
size      avg(ms)   bandwidth(GB/s)
65536     0.18      120
131072    0.28      95
262144    0.45      88
524288    1.6       90
1048576   2.9       60
2097152   6.5       25   <-- sharp drop
```
samir: looks like above ~1MB we lose multi-ring parallelism and fall back to a single stream pattern.
liam: thanks. my trace (nsys + nvprof sampling) shows long idle gaps on some ranks right after the first phase of reduce-scatter. compute overlap is poor.
perf-bot: perf trace uploaded: https://internal/perf/trace/1750456789 (contains timeline + per-rank nvtx)
kai: hypothesis: topology + NCCL algorithm choose a tree for those sizes or there is fragmentation causing ineffective chunking. options: force multi-ring, force tree, or implement application-level chunking to smaller sizes to keep rings busy.
marta: trying a hack: split tensors at 256KB per-chunk and pipeline chunk sends, got ~11% lower tail latency on my test. not perfect but promising.
samir: can you paste the patch?
marta: here — small change in allreduce launcher:
```
# pseudo
for tensor in tensors:
  chunks = split(tensor, chunk_size=256k)
  for c in chunks:
    ncclAllReduceAsync(c, ...)
  streamSynchronize(ordering_stream)
```
liam: interesting. we should also try forcing NCCL to use tree algo (if available) to compare. samir, can you run nccl-tests with env toggle (NCCL_ALGO=tree) on the same topology?
samir: on it. queued a 3-run batch with env toggles: ring (default), NCCL_ALGO=tree, and app-chunking. will post numbers.
kai: don't forget to run with IB disabled and socket-only to rule out NIC issues (NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1, NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0). we saw weird behavior once due to mixed interconnects.
perf-bot: quick note: the problematic jobs share a placement pattern: 2 nodes x 4 GPUs (nvlink within node, IB between nodes). might explain cross-node penalty at those msg sizes.
liam: next steps: 1) samir runs the env-matrix tests and posts numbers (ETA ~30m), 2) marta pushes a small benchmark harness that does chunked allreduce at app-level, 3) I'll try a nsight timeline focused on the reduce-scatter phases to check overlap gaps.
kai: if chunking fixes it we should consider adding an adaptive chunk-size heuristic in the runtime: pick chunk such that per-chunk size stays in high-bandwidth region. maybe 128K-256K based on these numbers.
samir: results posted: ring (default) median 2.9ms @1MB, tree median 2.1ms @1MB, app-chunking median 1.8ms @1MB. tree helps but chunking gives best overlap.
marta: nice. I'll prototype an adaptive rule: measure nccl microbench at startup, pick chunk = largest size with >80% peak bw, cap at 512K.
kai: good plan. file an RFC for runtime change (small heuristic + opt-out). raise PR and tag eng-runtime and eng-platform.
liam: logging: add an NVTX span around per-chunk enqueue so traces show chunk boundaries. will help debug regressions later.
perf-bot: created ticket INF-523: "TP all-reduce msgsize saturation — adaptive chunking heuristic" and assigned kai/marta/samir.
kai: thanks everyone. sync again if someone hits a counterexample (e.g., single-node 8-GPU that regresses). :thumbsup:
